chunks: 5314 - It was narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar that he said:
A man asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, while I was present, about a man who struck another man, and his urine did not stop.

He said: “If the urine continues until the night, then the diyyah is due upon him. If it continues until midday, then two-thirds of the diyyah is due upon him. If it continues until the rising of the day, then one-third of the diyyah is due upon him.”

key_terms.ارْتِفَاعِ النَّهَارِ: the rise of the day; an earlier daytime threshold used in assessing compensation
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money; financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine; here, the ongoing involuntary passing of urine caused by injury
key_terms.نِصْفِ النَّهَارِ: midday; a legal threshold used to determine the amount of compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for an injury that causes continuous urination?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on compensation for bodily injury when a blow causes continuous urination. The amount of diyyah varies according to the duration of the harm, showing a graded assessment of injury in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5314 - It was narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar that he said:
A man asked Abu Abdullah (as), while I was present, about a man who struck another man, causing his urine to flow continuously without stopping.

Imam (as) said: "If the urine continues until the night, then the full blood money (diyyah) is due. If it continues until midday, then two-thirds of the blood money is due. If it continues only until the morning rises, then one-third of the blood money is due."
